title: The impact of exposure to air pollution on cognitive performance

findings.antecedent: Longer-term mean API (Air Pollution Index) exposure
findings.mechanism: Changes in the brain chemistry or composition are likely more plausible channels between air pollution and cognition.
findings.source: Empirical Results text, SI Appendix, Table S1, Fig. 1A
findings.quote: all of the coefficients for mean APIs over a longer period are negative and statistically significant.

findings.antecedent: Longer-term mean API (Air Pollution Index) exposure
findings.mechanism: Changes in the brain chemistry or composition are likely more plausible channels between air pollution and cognition.
findings.source: Empirical Results text, SI Appendix, Table S1, Fig. 1B
findings.quote: all of the coefficients for mean APIs over a longer period are negative and statistically significant.

findings.antecedent: 1-d and 7-d mean API (Air Pollution Index) exposure
findings.source: Empirical Results text, SI Appendix, Table S1
findings.quote: Except for the effects of 1-d and 7-d air pollution exposure on math test scores... all of the coefficients for mean APIs over a longer period are negative and statistically significant.

findings.antecedent: 7-d-mean API (Air Pollution Index) increase by 1 SD
findings.source: Empirical Results text, SI Appendix, Table S1
findings.quote: an increase in the 7-d-mean API by 1 SD lowers verbal test scores by 0.278 point (0.026 SD)

findings.antecedent: Average API over 3 years before interview increase by 1 SD
findings.source: Empirical Results text, SI Appendix, Table S1
findings.quote: a 1 SD increase in average API over 3 y before the interview is associated with 1.132 points (0.108 SD) drop in verbal test scores.

findings.antecedent: Air pollution exposure
findings.consequent: Verbal test performance relative to Math test performance
findings.mechanism: Air pollution has a stronger effect on white matter (required more by verbal tests) than on gray matter (required more by math tests).
findings.source: Empirical Results text, SI Appendix, Table S1
findings.quote: air pollution exposure appears to exert a more negative effect on verbal test performance than math test performance.

findings.antecedent: Air pollution exposure (mean API) for men vs women
findings.mechanism: gender gap is likely caused by their different sizes of white matter activated, which can be reduced by air pollution.
findings.source: Empirical Results text, Fig. 1A, SI Appendix, Table S2a
findings.quote: Men are more vulnerable to air pollution than women. The gender difference is statistically significant, as shown by the asterisks in Fig. 1A.

findings.antecedent: Air pollution exposure (mean API) for men vs women
findings.mechanism: Air pollution has a stronger effect on white matter (required more by verbal tests) than on gray matter (required more by math tests).
findings.source: Empirical Results text, Fig. 1B, SI Appendix, Table S2b
findings.quote: As presented in Fig. 1B, the effect on math tests is more muted than that on verbal tests.

findings.antecedent: 3-y-mean API (Air Pollution Index) for older male cohorts (e.g., 65+)
findings.mechanism: cognitive decline or impairment are risk factors of Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia for elderly persons.
findings.source: Estimates of the Age-Cohort Effect... text, Fig. 2A, SI Appendix, Table S3
findings.quote: the negative effect on the verbal test performance is more pronounced for the older cohorts, especially among males.

findings.antecedent: 3-y-mean API (Air Pollution Index) for older cohorts
findings.source: Estimates of the Age-Cohort Effect... text, Fig. 2B, SI Appendix, Table S3
findings.quote: Such pattern, however, is less noticeable for the math tests.

findings.antecedent: 3-y-mean API (Air Pollution Index) for men over 44 y old with primary school education or below
findings.source: Estimates of the Age-Cohort Effect...by Educational Attainment text, Fig. 3A, SI Appendix, Table S4a
findings.quote: the effect for men over 44 y old with primary school education or below is highly negative.

findings.antecedent: 3-y-mean API (Air Pollution Index) for men aged 65 and above with middle school education or above
findings.source: Estimates of the Age-Cohort Effect...by Educational Attainment text, Fig. 3B, SI Appendix, Table S4a
findings.quote: the negative effect only shows up for men aged 65 and above.

findings.antecedent: 3-y-mean API (Air Pollution Index) for older women regardless of education
findings.source: Estimates of the Age-Cohort Effect...by Educational Attainment text, Fig. 3A/B
findings.quote: Such pattern, however, is not evident for older women regardless of their education.

findings.antecedent: Air pollution exposure (mean API) by educational attainment
findings.source: Estimates of the Age-Cohort Effect...by Educational Attainment text, SI Appendix, Table S4b
findings.quote: There is no clear difference [for math test scores by educational attainment].

findings.antecedent: API readings on days *after* cognitive tests
findings.source: Falsification Tests text, SI Appendix, Fig. S10
findings.quote: all of the coefficients are not statistically different from zero, largely dismissing the concern about potential omitted variables.

findings.antecedent: Air pollution exposure (API)
findings.source: Robustness text, SI Appendix, Table S13
findings.quote: None of the coefficients for API is significant, largely dismissing this channel.

findings.antecedent: Reducing PM10 concentration to US EPA standard (50 µg/m³)
findings.source: Interpretation text, Abstract
findings.quote: will on average lift verbal test scores by 2.41 points (or the movement of people from the median to the 63rd percentile in the verbal test distribution)

findings.antecedent: Reducing PM10 concentration to US EPA standard (50 µg/m³)
findings.source: Interpretation text, Abstract
findings.quote: and math test scores by 0.39 point (or the movement of people from the median to the 58th percentile in the math test distribution).

findings.antecedent: 1 SD decrease in 3-y-mean API for less educated men older than 64
findings.source: Interpretation text
findings.quote: A 1 SD decrease in 3-y-mean API leads to an increase in verbal test scores by 9.18 points (or the movement of people from the median to the 87th percentile in the verbal test distribution) for this group relative to the cohort younger than 25.

findings.antecedent: 1 SD decrease in 3-y-mean API for more educated older men
findings.source: Interpretation text
findings.quote: A 1 SD decrease in 3-y-mean API is associated with an increase in verbal test scores by 1.88 points (or the movement of people from the median to the 69th percentile in the verbal test distribution) for them relative to their younger counterpart.

limitations: The exact mechanism between air pollution and cognition (e.g., specific brain chemistry changes) is beyond the scope of this paper and left for future research.
